scope: Offline review of existing photographs and exact extracted firmware after owner asks to continue without disassembly. No console/programmer access, power operation, measurement, probe, firmware/configuration change or new router test.

identity.binding: Owner confirmed PHOTOS2 belongs to Router A on November 1; label readable in IMG_1296/1299/1301 and others. Native R0 identity independently corroborated in later boot records. This review does not newly query the router.

current_hardware_state: Last observed November 7 at 12:13:55 EST: A powered, assembled, battery installed, same 230 W brick/AP on port 4/RJ45 connected, all test/programmer wiring removed, console released. No hardware interaction during this review. Historical bare-board/battery-removed photos are not the current state.

photo_attribution.review: All 12 originals visually reviewed; overview/connector edge and component-side closeups. No underside view in this set.
Existing C8300 photo index plus current visual inspection of IMG_1304/1305/1306. IMG_1310 is the indexed C8300-1N1S-4T2X front-panel view.
Remain relevant to this PoE investigation; do not describe all PHOTOS3 as unrelated. PSU label evidence remains supply-label.json from November 6.

photo_attribution.identity: Historical Arata board FOC28292GX9, not A board FOC28292GUQ
photo_attribution.review: Visually reviewed for comparison only. Do not use this underside view to establish A component population or electrical state. Historical attribution correction retained.

photo_observations.finding: White connector J3300 beside/behind the RJ45 bank is fitted and empty; no daughterboard is attached to it in these photographs. J3300 designator is readable in IMG_1297 and IMG_1299.
photo_observations.limit: Connector purpose, pinout, and whether it is the production PoE daughter-card connector are not established by position or appearance. These are historical photographs.

photo_observations.finding: Board label FOC28292GUQ binds the detailed component-side views to the established A photo set.

No physical PSE-controller part number is confidently identified from the reviewed A photos. Thermal interface material covers some component markings, and this set lacks the underside. Photo review does not prove absence of integrated/equivalent PoE circuitry.

firmware_review.trace: cpa_sb_arata_platform_init copies the PoE Daughter Card label at 0x114c-0x11a0 and the Poe Daughter Module label at 0x1728-0x175c into platform descriptors. These are Arata-specific modeled objects, not merely a generic package filename.
firmware_review.additional_observation: arata.lua lines 33-36 define one internal and one external PoE slot and POE_EXT_EEPROM=false. Generic ngswitch routines invoke dev_legolas_poe_create; an Arata-specific controller selection/part number was not established by this review.
firmware_review.limits: No library or Lua was loaded/executed. Firmware inclusion and descriptors do not prove hardware population, device communication, initialization, or a valid J3300 mapping. Prior Si3470A package hash match remains file-integrity evidence only.

references.finding: Cisco documents a PoE daughter card supplied when the PoE PSU is selected at initial order, not field-upgradeable. Production description does not prove prototype population or J3300 function.

Downloaded and inspected Cisco illustrations 527261.jpg/527264.jpg; these do not identify J3300 or a PSE controller. Cached unmodified in ignored tmp/c8235-photo-review-20261107. No disassembly instructions executed.

assessment: Existing photos support continued identification without opening the router. An absent optional PoE board is a supported hypothesis from empty J3300, owner report, Arata descriptors and production documentation, but physical absence of all required circuitry and the cause of zero status flags remain unverified. No software-only repair has been established.
next: Continue offline correlation of the exact Arata built-in PoE driver/presence path and reference hardware. A targeted controller read requires a verified controller/protocol/address first; no blind bus scan, forced presence/power flag, repeat crashing native get or disassembly selected. Same brick ISR4321/AP success remains valid; no resistor retest.
